items.title: Authoritarian leaders facing setbacks, says M.K. Muneer
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is destined to meet the fate of Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini, M.K.
Muneer, chairperson of the Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission, has said.
He was inaugurating the delegates’ meet organised as part of the Keralam State conference of the Muslim Youth League here on Saturday (November 7).
Mr. Muneer said the people are living in an era when authoritarian leaders are facing setbacks.
“That is why Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu are being forced to confront resistance.
They will ultimately meet the same fate as Hitler and Mussolini.

Shweta Bhatt, wife of former IPS officer Sanjiv Bhatt, who was the chief guest at the delegates’ meet, said that the legal battle and imprisonment of her husband have entered its eighth year, but the family will not retreat from its struggle for truth and…
Muslim Youth League State president Panakkad Syed Munavvar Ali Shihab Thangal presided over the meeting.

items.title: Health Minister U.T. Khader sets up fresh panel to review treatment of infant who suffered brain damage at private hospital
points: The 14-month-old boy was taken to Cloudnine Hospital on July 26 for emergency surgical repair of a full-thickness ear laceration. | Image for representation only | Photo Credit: shapecharge Karnataka Health Minister U.T.

Khader has constituted a fresh expert committee comprising doctors from NIMHANS, the Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health (IGICH) and the State Health Department to review the treatment of an infant who suffered severe brain damage following an ear…
The move follows a meeting between the infant’s family and Mr. Khader on Thursday (November 5), when they sought justice and demanded that the hospital take responsibility for the infant’s treatment.

Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Khader said the government wanted the infant to recover and return home in good health, but the immediate priority was to ensure that he received the best possible medical care.
The 14-month-old boy, son of Sampath Kumar K.P. of Kattedoddi village in Mandya district, was taken to Cloudnine Hospital on July 26 for emergency surgical repair of a full-thickness ear laceration.

items.title: Music and yoga strike a healing chord behind prison walls in Keralam’s Viyyur Central Prison
points: ‘Aathmanadam’ a music-yoga programme organised at the Viyyur Central Prison to promote the mental and emotional well-being of inmates.

Music and yoga came together to offer a soothing break from prison routine at Viyyur Central Prison and Correctional Home, where 40 inmates and 10 staff members took part in an interactive wellness programme titled ‘Aathmanadam’ .
Organised under the direction of prison superintendent Venu K., the programme sought to promote the mental and emotional well-being of inmates through the therapeutic power of music and yoga.
Meharuf Raj, patron of the Aathmanadam organisation and a noted music therapist, inaugurated the event and led a music therapy session recently.
Music transcended the prison walls as participants joined in songs that brought moments of joy and emotional engagement.
The event was held on the fifth day of the Malayalam Language Week celebrations at the prison, with the participation of inmates interested in music and yoga.
Regional Welfare Officer (Central Zone) T.G.
Central prison welfare officer Saji Simon and Basil Elias also spoke.

items.title: Free Risdiplam for SMA patients to be made available in all districts
points: The government will make Risdiplam medicine for patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) available through Medical colleges in all districts, Health Minister K.
The Additional Chief Secretary (Health) has been entrusted with the task of coordinating the initiative, the Minister said in a statement here on Saturday.
Decentralised distribution of Risdiplam will ensure easier access to treatment and continuity of care, while providing relief to patients and their families.
The government seeks to establish a new model of healthcare which will address the needs of all families affected by the disease, he said.
At present, free medication is distributed only through the SMA clinics at the Thiruvananthapuram and Kozhikode Government Medical colleges.
Taking these hardships of families into account, the government has decided to make the medication available through the Paediatrics departments of all Medical colleges, Mr. Muraleedharan said.
Free medication is currently available only for patients up to 12 years of age.

items.title: JSP stronger after 100% strike rate in ULBs: party leader Daneti Sridhar
points: Leaders and activists of various parties and organisations joined JSP in the presence of Dr. Sridhar and JSP-Srikakulam Mayor candidate Daneti Radha Rani in a meeting organised in Srikakulam.
Speaking to media on the occasion, he said that JSP would win Srikakulam municipal corporation for which the election would be held very soon.
Dr. Radha Rani said that the people had completely rejected YSRCP in local body elections and the voters would repose their faith only on NDA in ensuing Srikakulam corporation elections.
During seats’ allocation, JSP got Srikakulam corporation but the election was postponed as legal procedures needed to completed after merger of nearby villages with the Corporation.

items.title: JSP candidate dies before vote counting, wins MPTC seat in East Godavari district
points: Jana Sena Party (JSP) MPTC candidate Garapati Divya, who died of cardiac arrest a few hours before vote counting, registered a victory with a majority of 361 votes at Damanthunigidem panchayat of Devarapalli mandal in East Godavari district.
The 28-year-old was admitted to a private hospital immediately on Friday evening after she complained of chest pain.
By Friday night, she was declared dead due to cardiac arrest while undergoing treatment.
The JSP candidate secured 969 votes, while her rival, G.
Dhanalakshmi of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), received 608 votes.
Ms. Divya’s last rites were performed while the counting of the votes was in progress.
Scores of Jana Sena supporters joined in Ms. Divya’s last rites.

items.title: I PU question papers to be set at State level in Karnataka
points: The question papers will be prepared by the Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board.
However, the examinations will be conducted under the supervision of the Department of School Education (Pre-University).
The State government issued an order to this effect on Saturday.
A uniform examination timetable applicable to all PU colleges across the State will be prepared for the conduct of these examinations.
On the day of the examination, the question papers will be transmitted to the colleges in a digital format.
Although the question papers will be prepared at the State level, the evaluation process will continue to take place at the college level.
The results will be published only after they have been reviewed and approved by the respective Deputy Director Pre-University of the district.

items.title: A half-century of rhythm: T.R. Chandran from Thrissur, a constant at Chembai Sangeetholsavam
points: Chandran and his wife, Sathi, music has been a lifelong source of strength, purpose and joy.
A resident of Thichur in Thrissur district, Chandran has an unbroken association with the Chembai Sangeetholsavam at Guruvayur since 1977.
As the festival celebrates its golden jubilee, his uninterrupted participation for 49 years stands out as a remarkable musical journey.

A Ganabhushanam graduate of the Chembai Memorial Music College, Palakkad, Chandran served as a music teacher at the Guruvayur Devaswom’s Sree Krishna Higher Secondary School for 29 years, retiring in 2006.
Yet, he continued teaching without interruption, commuting from Thichur to Guruvayur, often changing two or three buses.
He first performed the Swathi Thirunal composition at the festival in 1977.
Music College, taught music at Pengamukku High School for 31 years.
Chandran’s wish remains simple: to continue offering his musical prayers before Guruvayurappan at the Chembai Mandapam.

The organisation called for comprehensive electoral reforms, including proportional representation, measures to curb money and muscle power, and legalisation of State funding of elections to restore and strengthen the democratic system.
PASIR will also launch a nationwide campaign, Reclaim Our Democracy, from November 26 to December 20.

items.title: Declare November 7 as State Students’ Day, urges Vice-Chancellor
points: Ambedkar first entered school. | Photo Credit: File photo Bangalore University Vice-Chancellor C.
Shivaraju has requested the Karnataka government to declare November 7, the day Dr. B.R.
Ambedkar first entered school, as State Students’ Day and celebrate it across Karnataka.
Speaking at the Students’ Day celebration organised by the Babasaheb Dr. B.R.
Ambedkar Central Library at Bangalore University, Prof.
“His life and achievements stand as an inspiration to students, demonstrating the importance of education in overcoming social barriers and achieving excellence,” he said.

Referring to Maharashtra, where November 7 is observed as Students’ Day, he said Bangalore University would submit a request to the Karnataka government to introduce a similar celebration across the State on the day.
Central Library Librarian Raghunandan said Bangalore University had initiated a signature campaign to support the demand.

items.title: KLDB to launch livestock research centre at Mattupetty
points: Cattles at the KLDB center at Mattuppetty near Munnar in Idukki | Photo Credit: Sandeep Vellaram The Kerala Livestock Development Board (KLDB) is set to establish the Centre for Advancement in Livestock Productivity and Research (CALPR) at Mattupetty near…
Officials said the facility marks a key step toward ensuring the long-term growth and sustainability of the State’s livestock sector.
Minister for Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development Bindu Krishna will inaugurate the centre on Monday (November 9) at 11 a.m.

In addition to offering research and training facilities for farmers, scientists, researchers, professionals, entrepreneurs, and startups, joint research initiatives will be launched in partnership with national and international institutions.

The centre will also ensure dedicated training and research opportunities for women, Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities, rural tribal farmers, and economically disadvantaged groups.
The Minister will also launch the newly developed Herd Management Software (HMS) for the KLDB.
Officials pointed out that the board currently relies on a Livestock Management Software (LMS) system developed roughly 25 years ago.

items.title: Sharmila hails Congress performance in Chirala civic polls
points: Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Y.S.
Sharmila has congratulated former MLA and senior Congress leader Amanchi Krishna Mohan on the party’s performance in the Chirala Municipality elections, in which it won 10 of the 44 councillor seats.

In a statement, Ms. Sharmila praised Mr. Krishna Mohan, who is also the Bapatla District Congress Committee president and a member of the State Political Affairs Committee (PAC), for his efforts to strengthen the party in Chirala.
The Congress contested 42 wards and secured second place in several others.

Describing the party’s performance as a moral victory, Ms. Sharmila said the results demonstrated the Congress’s potential to emerge as a political alternative, despite failing to capture control of the municipality.
The Chirala Municipality elections were part of the 2026 Andhra Pradesh urban local body polls.
Polling was held on November 1, while counting took place on November 6 after being postponed due to adverse weather conditions caused by Cyclone Murasu.

items.title: Pralhad Joshi accuses Karnataka government of burdening people with price hikes
points: Union Minister for Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi has accused the Congress government in Karnataka of burdening people with repeated price increases.

Addressing a press conference here on Saturday, Mr. Joshi alleged that While the Congress government made tall claims about helping the people through the five guarantee schemes, it was actually snatching away the benefits with frequent price hikes.

“Petrol and diesel prices have been increased three times and bus fares twice,” he said, adding that the government had effected hike of 10% in water tariffs, 25% in sewerage charges, 20% in liquor prices and 50% in licence fees.
He claimed that increases in various taxes and charges were expected to generate an additional annual revenue of ₹60,000 crore for the government.

The projected revenue included ₹6,000 crore from petrol and diesel price increases, ₹1,000 crore from bus fare revision, ₹3,712 crore from vehicle registration fees, ₹450 crore from metro fares and ₹5,000 crore from revisions in property guideline values.

items.title: MG Tomahawk EV’s Sales Triple; 8 In 10 Cars Sold By MG In India Are Electric
points: MG's Hector Tomahawk EV recorded 1,545 registrations in October 2026, compared with 443 in September.
More significantly, electric cars accounted for roughly 84% of all MG passenger vehicle registrations during October, showing how much the company's sales now depend on battery-powered models.
MG registered 5,965 electric cars during October, up 8% from 5,521 in September and 11.3% from 5,360 a year earlier.
The Essence seven-seater alone accounted for 1,000 registrations, or nearly 65% of Tomahawk sales.
The Tomahawk was ninth among electric car models during October, with roughly 4.2% of all electric passenger vehicle registrations.
Its 1,545 units placed it behind Mahindra's XEV 9S and XEV 9e, the Tata Sierra EV and even Mahindra's BE 6, which recorded around 1,555 units in the same ElecTree data collection.
MG raised the ex-showroom price of every Tomahawk EV variant by Rs 75,000 after the introductory offer ended, taking the range from Rs 20.25 lakh to Rs 24.25 lakh.

Addressing a press conference here on Saturday, vedike district president Manjunath Nalwarkar said that Sumit Rajashekar Hosalli, a native of Chittapur taluk, who is pursuing an ITI course in Kalaburagi, was allegedly assaulted by five fellow inmates on…

items.title: NDA continues its winning streak, set to crush YSRCP in ZPTC and MPTC elections as well
points: A TDP candidate who won the MPTC election celebrates her victory along with supporters in Vijayawada on Saturday. | Photo Credit: G.N.

RAO The TDP and it’s allies, the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the BJP, continued their stellar performance in the elections to the Zilla and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs and MPTCs) after crushing the YSRCP in the Urban Local Body (ULB)…
Polling was conducted for 582 ZPTCs and 7,767 MPTCs in 28 districts on November 5 following the declaration of 77 and 2,051 ZPTCs and MPTCs respectively as unanimously elected.

The TDP-led ruling coalition was far ahead in the race in both the ZPTCs and MPTCs, winning in over 320 ZPTCs, including 77 that had been declared as unanimously elected, and leading in nearly 100 ZPTCs.
A similar picture was unfolding in the 7,767 MPTCs at the time of of fling this report.

items.title: Women from Wanaparthy villages get trained in japa care
points: The first batch of women from Wanaparthy in Telangana were trained in various aspects of attending to needs to mothers and newborns, at the Rural Self Employment Training Institute (RSETI) in Wanaparthy.
The increasing migration to cities alongside working couples who live away from families created some gaps in care-giving for people in old age, toddlers and mothers and their newborns.
The first batch of 36 women bagged jobs with a monthly salary of ₹20,000 to take care of mothers and newborns in Hyderabad and Bengaluru.

They were trained at Rural Self Employment Training Institute (RSETI) in taking care of newborns, aiding mothers in recovery, hygiene, preparation of nutritious post-natal diet, communication, customer relations and financial literacy.

Since Japa care does not figure among the regular courses prescribed for RSETIs, UBI RSETI Wanaparthy approached and received a ₹6.9 lakh grant for the programme from NABARD under its Livelihood and Enterprise Development Programme (LEDP).

items.title: NDA dominates rural local body polls in Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts
points: Updated - November 07, 2026 08:48 pm IST - VIZIANAGARAM/SRIKAKULAM Majji Siri Sahasra, who won the Terlam ZPTC seat, presents a bouquet to Bobbili MLA Baby Nayana in Vizianagaram district on Saturday.
The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and its alliance partners continued their winning streak in Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts in the rural local body elections held on Saturday.
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which suffered a setback in the urban local body elections, put up a relatively better performance, winning a sizeable number of seats in several mandals.
However, the ruling NDA alliance secured more than 70% of the ZPTC and MPTC seats in the two districts.
In Vizianagaram district, the TDP and its alliance partners won a majority of the 27 ZPTC seats.
The ruling alliance registered emphatic victories in Rajam, Bobbili, Gajapathinagaram and several other Assembly constituencies, winning more than 90% of the seats in some segments.
TDP MLA Baby Nayana congratulated her and other newly elected local body representatives at his office in Bobbili Fort.

items.title: Multiple Elector Photo Identity Cards generated for same person during SIR, admits Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer
points: The report highlighted instances of people holding multiple voter IDs within Mahadevapura, as well as cases where the same Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number appeared in the final electoral rolls of two different Assembly constituencies.
In response, the CEO’s office said that during the SIR, some applicants had submitted multiple Form 6 applications (seeking inclusion) through the Citizen Service Portal.
As these applications were “processed independently”, multiple EPIC numbers were inadvertently generated for the same individual.

Clarifying how identical EPIC numbers appeared in the final rolls of two constituencies, the CEO’s office said that in some cases, Form 8 applications seeking migration to another constituency had been approved and the electors’ names incorporated into the…
However, the corresponding Form 7 applications seeking deletion of their names from the previous constituencies remained pending.
The Hindu had highlighted seven such cases, involving 14 entries where the same EPIC ID number was issued in two different constituencies.

This follows discussions with the Chief Minister on the matter.
At present, ethanol blend of more than the prescribed level of 20% in petrol has not come to the attention of authorities in the State.
Detection of high ethanol blend percentages in petrol sold in Karnataka led to the decision to conduct inspections in Keralam.
Samples will be collected from various places in Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode, and Kannur districts for the inspection.

A notification brought out by the State in 2014 according to the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, gives officials from the Civil Supplies Commissioner to the taluk supply…

items.title: Supreme Court says stopping vehicles, construction to prevent pollution ‘old, tried, failed tools’
points: Vehicles stuck in traffic on the Delhi-Gurugram Expressway amid hazy conditions, in Gurugram, on November 6, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed measures like banning vehicles and construction to curb air…

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked the Union government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) if they had any “significant scientific method other than stopping vehicles and stopping construction”.
Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, arguing for CAQM and the Centre, said that it would not be completely true to call such measures a “complete failure”.
Ms. Bhati said emergency and pre-emptive measures like Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) have at least been able to arrest air pollution at sustainable levels.
“But yet the Air Quality Index (AQI) is touching 400...” the Chief Justice responded.
Let us not talk about a utopia where the AQI would become 100 or less,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the three-judge Bench, addressed the CAQM.

items.title: Mutton Feast, Rolls Of Tape: How Cab Driver Killed Wife, Relatives In Bengaluru
points: The cab driver who allegedly murdered his wife and six members of her family meticulously planned the killings, feeding them mutton laced with sleeping pills and bludgeoning them to death.
Before inviting the next victim for their last lunch, he would wrap the bodies of the previous victims in adhesive tape to trap the stench.
The accused, Indushekhar, had been married to Sunitha for nearly two decades and lived with her in Bengaluru's Rajajinagar area.
Investigators probing the horrific Rajajinagar serial killings have uncovered a chillingly calculated modus operandi allegedly adopted by Indushekhar.
According to sources, Indushekhar would allegedly invite his victims home during the afternoon, prepare a mutton meal, and serve them food and alcohol laced with sleeping pills.
After the murders, he would wrap the bodies tightly in multiple layers of adhesive tape, reportedly as many as 10 layers, to prevent blood leakage and contain the smell of decomposition.

items.title: 'Patiala Peg', 3 Other Songs Banned From Diljit Dosanjh's Indore Concert
points: Child protection authorities in Indore have directed the management of C-21 Mall to make sure singer Diljit Dosanjh does not sing four of his songs at his live concert at the venue on November 15.

The notice, dated November 6 and issued by the District Child Protection Officer as part of the Women and Child Development Department, Indore, lists four songs: 'Patiala Peg', '5 Taara'', 'Jeeb Vicho Afeem' ('Case') and 'Jatt Uthe Fire Karda', all in Punjabi.
It directs the mall management, "in compliance with" a July 2019 order of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, to ensure the songs are not sung during the concert.
On October 21, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal informed organiser BookMyShow Live that permission for the concert had been declined.

items.title: Telangana plans modern storage infra for paddy to protect ryots’ interests
points: Building a scientific silos network would act as a major long-term intervention to protect the interests of paddy farmers, Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N.
Uttam Kumar Reddy said at a meeting held here on Saturday to review paddy procurement and to discuss two proposed models for establishing the silo infrastructure.
Under the first model, the Telangana State Civil Supplies Corporation (TSCSC) would directly establish silos in a big way by mobilising loans from reputed financial institutions.
In the second model, modern storage capacity would be created through private sector participation, the Minister explained.

“The government will encourage private entrepreneurs to establish silo facilities at about 20 locations to be identified across the State initially with the Civil Supplies Corporation providing a rental guarantee to make the investments financially…
The Minister instructed the authorities to finalise the proposals expeditiously, including the financial implications, financing arrangements and rental commitments.

items.title: Vande Mataram resonates across key landmarks of Mysuru
points: In a unique initiative, Purna Chetana School brought together 16 students from Classes 3 to 8 to render all stanzas of the national song.
The students first rendered the song at Chamundi Hills at 8.30 a.m., followed by Mysuru palace and Kukkarahalli Lake.
The initiative aimed to create awareness among the public, particularly the younger generation, about the historical significance of ‘Vande Mataram’ and its role in the freedom movement.
As the students’ rendition filled the surroundings with patriotic fervour, several members of the public joined them in singing, while visitors stood in respect, the school said in a press release.
The performance also drew the attention of tourists at Mysuru palace.
CEO Darshan Raj, CAO Maadhurya Ramaswamy and senior teacher Ramya accompanied the students during the rendition.

items.title: Murder accused shot at by police in Vijayapura
points: The police shot at Sameer Mulla, the prime accused in the murder of Yaseen Zuberi, after he allegedly opened fire at a police team with a country-made pistol and attempted to escape arrest in Vijayapura.

Speaking to press persons in Vijayapura on Saturday, Superintendent of Police Lakshman Nimbargi said that four persons had already been arrested in connection with the murder, while efforts were under way to apprehend two other accused.
The police had gone to arrest Mulla when he allegedly opened fire at them with a country-made pistol and attempted to flee.
Despite being warned, he continued to resist, prompting the police to shoot him in the right leg and take him into custody, Mr. Nimbargi said.
The injured was admitted to the district hospital for treatment.
Investigation had revealed that six persons were involved in the murder, Mr. Nimbargi said, adding that the police had obtained leads about the remaining accused.
The police were also investigating the source of the country-made pistol used in the incident, he said.

items.title: TDP-led alliance extends winning streak in NTR district local body polls
points: A TDP candidate celebrates her victory in the MPTC elections with party supporters in Vijayawada on Saturday. | Photo Credit: G.N.

Rao The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and its allies, the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), continued their winning run in NTR district in the elections to rural local bodies, following their landslide victory in the recent urban local…
Counting of votes polled in elections to 276 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and 16 Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) seats began at 8 a.m. on Saturday.
Lakshmisha said in a statement that the counting process was conducted peacefully.
As of 7 p.m., counting had been completed in 206 of the 276 MPTC seats.
The TDP won 151 seats, while the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) secured 36.
Of the 16 ZPTC seats, TDP candidates had been declared elected in five constituencies — Chandarlapadu, G.
Konduru, Ibrahimpatnam, Reddigudem and Tiruvuru — as of 7 p.m.

items.title: P.E.S. College of Engineering awards degrees to 972 students
points: A total of 972 students, including 829 undergraduate and 143 postgraduate students, received their degrees at the 17th Graduation Day of P.E.S.
College of Engineering in Mandya on Saturday.
The degrees were awarded to students of the 2025-26 academic year at the ceremony presided over by People’s Education Trust (R) president K.S.
Addressing the graduates, Mr. Anand stressed the need to embrace technological advancements while remaining rooted in cultural heritage, ethical values and traditions.
He said students should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications and focus on research, innovation, entrepreneurship and skill development to keep pace with emerging technologies.

Chidananda Gowda, former Vice-Chancellor of Kuvempu University, called upon graduates to strengthen their understanding of fundamental concepts and technical knowledge while making responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Eight undergraduate and four postgraduate first-rank holders for 2025-26 were felicitated at the ceremony.
Shankare Gowda Endowment Medals for overall first rank were awarded to Sudarshan K.

items.title: No respite from deluge even a week after rain: Residents of Palakol complain
points: Housing Board Colony, Allu Venkata Satnarsyana Colony and the neighbouring areas were inundated.
Flood entered many houses and damaged household articles,” said residents of Housing Board Colony.
As colonies were flooded, there has been no proper power supply, and streets remained inaccessible for milk and vegetable vendors, residents complained.
Floodwater in the colonies has not receded, and snakes and poisonous reptiles were creating panic, said a resident, Vijaya Lakshmi.
“We have sent messages through social media groups to the Palakol Municipal and Revenue officials, and tried in vain to meet the public representatives.
There has been no response from them,” said Sathi Babu of AVS Colony.

“Medicines and essentials are exhausted in several houses, and senior citizens, pregnant and lactating women were suffering, as the colonies are in knee-deep water,” Kumari, a resident whose house was damaged due to the cyclone, told The Hindu on Saturday.
No steps have been taken to drain out the floodwater, a Kirana shop owner said.

items.title: CITU adds 4.5 lakh members in Keralam, plans digital membership mapping
points: The Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) has launched a massive exercise to digitise its membership across Keralam, its national general secretary Elamaram Kareem said on Saturday.

Addressing the media on the sidelines of the CITU State conference in Kottayam, Mr. Kareem said the organisation was also working to map the total number of workers in different sectors across the State digitally.
The initiative, in keeping with changing times and advances in technology, would help the trade union assess its organisational strength and identify areas that needed improvement, he said.
The CITU has enrolled around 4.5 lakh workers in Keralam since its previous State conference in 2021, he added.
The leadership is also planning to mobilise 20,000 workers from Keralam for a massive rally in Delhi during the first three days of December to protest against the four labour codes.
Meanwhile, sources said Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat member K.K.

items.title: Revanth Reddy’s Praja Balam tour after Sankranthi
points: Revanth Reddy announced the launch of ‘Praja Balam’ (People’s strength) programme after the Sankranthi festival, where he would visit every village to meet people and farmers to interact with them.

Addressing a meeting of progressive farmers and agriculture scientists at Hakimpet in Vikarabad district on Saturday, he said all the MLAs and MLCs would be with the farmers interacting with them in the light of El Nino conditions.
“It is our responsibility to be with the farmers and guide them when they are going through a tough time due to El Nino,” he said.
The Chief Minister urged the farmers’ support in tackling the El Nino by staying away from water-intensive crops in the Rabi season.
‘Don’t get influenced by the opposition parties and go for paddy and waste your money.
Instead, heed the government’s appeal and cultivate dry crops and vegetables to earn money,” he said.

items.title: Agents booked, five fertility centres named in Hyderabad’s illegal oocyte racket; Telangana Women’s Commission questions inaction
points: The alleged exploitation came to light after 43 women were rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad.

Women from economically weaker sections were allegedly offered between ₹20,000 and ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the racket reportedly made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.

Expressing strong displeasure over the delay, the Commission said that despite its directions to the concerned authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the hospitals and laboratories allegedly involved, no concrete steps had been taken…

During her interaction with the affected women, Commission Chairperson Nerella Sharada said that she was informed about the alleged involvement of five institutions which include, Indira IVF Centre, Narmada Fertility Centre, Oasis Fertility Centre, Sadguru…
The women also named an individual identified as Dr. Hussain in their complaints.
Ms. Nerella expressed concern over the fact that the whereabouts of Dr. Hussain remain unknown and that no case has been registered against him so far.

items.title: Prakash G.T. Nittali takes charge as Shivamogga DC

Nittali assumed charge as the Deputy Commissioner of Shivamogga on Saturday, taking over from Prabhulinga Kavalikatti.

Mr. Kavalikatti, a 2013-batch IAS officer, had taken charge as the Deputy Commissioner in January this year and served in the post for about 11 months.

items.title: NDA grabs 117 MPTC seats in Bapatla district, TDP wins 109
points: The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), registered a decisive victory in the MPTC elections in Bapatla district by winning 117 seats of the 273 MPTCs taken…
According to the updates received till the last report came in on Saturday, the TDP secured 109 MPTC seats, while its alliance partner JSP won eight.
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) secured 19 seats, while others won one.

The TDP dominated several mandals, securing 17 seats in Martur, 12 in Parchur, 11 in Bhattiprolu, 10 in Repalle, nine in Chinaganjam, eight each in Karamchedu and Nagaram, seven in Yeddanapudi, six each in Cherukupalli and P.V.
Palem, four in Nizampatnam, three in Bapatla, two each in Amruthalur and Tsundur, and one each in Chirala, Karlapalem, Kolluru and Vemuru.
The JSP won three seats in Repalle, two each in Cherukupalli and Karlapalem, and one each in Chinaganjam and the remaining mandal as reflected in the district tally, taking its total to eight.

items.title: After Karnataka Charge, Centre Says E20 Petrol Meets Prescribed Standards
points: The 56 samples tested in Karnataka, covering different locations and all three oil marketing companies (OMCs), recorded ethanol content of 19-20 per cent, averaging 19.30 per cent, the ministry said.

The findings directly contradict a recent press release by Karnataka's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, which claimed that petrol samples collected from certain retail outlets in the state contained 26-31 per cent…

The three OMCs have questioned the sampling and testing procedures adopted in Karnataka's October 2026 exercise, arguing that the reported results cannot be independently validated without compliance with prescribed statutory procedures and disclosure of…

Under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, six one-litre samples must be drawn during an inspection.

Under IS 17021:2018, amended in August 2025, ethanol content must be determined through specified methods, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, water extraction or Gas Chromatography under prescribed ASTM standards.

items.title: Assam Woman Says Congress Leader Assaulted Her, Demands DNA Test Of Son
points: Highlighting claims of alleged sexual exploitation against senior Congress leader Harak Singh Rawat, Assam resident Indira Devi (alias Jenny) has demanded a new DNA test to establish paternity and secure her son's legal entitlement to his father's name.
In an exclusive conversation with ANI on Saturday, Jenny alleged that she was taken to Rawat's residence in Yamuna Colony in 2002 by one of his party workers when she was 16 years old.
Accusing the Congress leader, she alleged, "This is from back in 2002.
In 2002, in Yamuna Colony, I used to work at an STD booth.
From that STD booth, one of his party workers took me to Harak Singh Rawat's house in Yamuna Colony.
The 'Jenny episode' is a decades-old political controversy in Uttarakhand that first surfaced in 2003.
Jenny had given birth to a child at a government hospital in Dehradun in June 2003 and had claimed that Rawat was the child's father.

items.title: ₹90 dividend per share: This stock announces 900% payout - Do you own? Payment, record date, returns
points: Dividend record date ahead: Shares of Bayer CropScience Limited will remain in focus next week due to the upcoming record date for its ₹90 per equity share dividend payout.
Bayer CropScience Limited share price closed 0.45% higher on Friday, after seeing 1.64% jump over the last five trading sessions.
The company’s board of directors, on Tuesday, November 3, announced an interim dividend of ₹90 per equity share with a face value of ₹10 each (ie 900% of the face value) for FY27.
The board fixed Thursday, November 12, as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for the payout.
As per the company’s BSE filing, the board will disburse the dividend payout among investors by Monday, November 30, 2026.
Alongside announcement of dividend, the company also reported a net profit of ₹166.2 crore in the second quarter of FY27, against ₹152.7 crore reported in the year ago period.
The stock closed 0.45% higher at ₹3316.50 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of ₹14,905.04 crore on Friday.

items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls pleading with Rajiv not to become PM after Indira’s assassination: ‘They will kill you’
points: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi pleaded with her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, not to become India's prime minister following the assassination of his mother, Indira Gandhi, on October 31, 1984.

In an edited extract from her memoir published by The Guardian, Sonia recounts the emotional moments after Indira Gandhi was shot dead by her bodyguards at her 1, Safdarjung Road residence in New Delhi.
Rajiv Gandhi was in West Bengal, attending a political rally, when he was informed that a serious incident had taken place in Delhi.
He rushed back to the national capital and landed at around 3.30 pm before being driven straight to the hospital.
Recalling their meeting at the hospital, Sonia said she longed to be alone with her husband for a moment.
Sonia said she was overwhelmed by anger and anguish at the prospect of Rajiv taking over as prime minister, fearing that he too could become a target.

items.title: Death Count In Delhi Building Collapse Rises To 6, All Victims Identified
points: The death count in the building collapse incident in Delhi's Chawri Bazar area has risen to six, with all the victims identified, officials said on Saturday.

The six victims have been identified as Sanjeet Kumar, Kishori Sah, Pankaj Sharma, Vipin Ram, Shantu and Dinesh Sah, according to the latest update issued during the ongoing rescue operations at the collapse site, according to the police.
Five of the victims hailed from Bihar, while Vipin Ram was a resident of Saket Block in Mandawali, Fazilpur, Delhi.
On Thursday, the three-storey under-construction building collapsed at Gali Sheesh Mahal, Gali Shehatara, near Ajmeri Gate, in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar area at around 10:30 am.

Three contractors have been arrested in connection with the collapse of an under-construction building in Delhi's Chawri Bazar area, which claimed two lives, as rescue operations continued on Friday to locate people feared trapped beneath the debris, Delhi…
The arrested contractors have been identified as Siraj, Tajuddin and Furkan, all residents of Village Sirohi, Tehsil Dauj, in Haryana's Faridabad district.

items.title: 'I Am God, Obey Me': Woman Accuses Vrindavan-Based Preacher Indradev Of Sexual Assault
points: Kashimira police station in Mira-Bhayandar registered a Zero FIR transferable to Mathura, where the alleged crime took place.
At a press conference held by an activist and the woman, there were other women too who made accusations, though so far there's one FIR.
The complainant in that FIR alleged that Indradev called her to his room late at night while she was staying at his Sevadham Ashram in Vrindavan in 2023.
The woman further alleged that the preacher made her undress during video calls, performed obscene acts and recorded them.
According to the complaint, the woman came into contact with Indradev in 2023 after watching his discourses on social media.
The woman said she had been trying to get justice for several months, but her complaint had been ignored in Mathura.
The Zero FIR was registered after activist Trupti Desai, who leads an organisation called Bhumata Brigade, intervened.
Desai appealed to any other woman wronged by the preacher to come forward without fear and file a complaint.

items.title: Ghaziabad outpost blast: Agencies conduct checks; social media account claims responsibility
points: A day after an explosion damaged the rear wall of the Vasundhara police outpost in Ghaziabad, several agencies, including the anti-terror squad, bomb disposal unit and forensic teams, conducted checks and collected evidence from the site on Saturday,…
The explosion that happened on Friday around 9pm at the rear wall of the Vasundhara police outpost cracked walls and shattered windowpanes.
A food delivery worker sustained minor injuries in the incident, police said on Saturday.
“Pieces of glass hit the head of the food delivery person, aged about 20 years, following the explosion.
There was no fire resulting from the incident,” Rijul, DCP of the Trans-Hindon zone, told HT on Saturday morning.

Later on Saturday, several agencies, including the anti-terror squad, bomb disposal unit, and forensic and field unit teams, visited the affected outpost and conducted checks to ascertain the cause of the explosion.
Meanwhile, a social media account operating under the handle GHAZI 2 (@cuhmfu40pn60793) claimed responsibility for the explosion at the police outpost and issued threats in a post.

items.title: Q2 results race: Samvardhana Motherson vs Uno Minda - Which auto ancillary stock scores better? Revenue, profit, target
points: Samvardhana Motherson vs Uno Minda: Two of the most widely tracked auto ancillary firms, Uno Minda and Samvardhana Motherson International recently announced their second quarter results for the financial year 2026-27.
While Samvardhana Motherson reported 42% year-on-year jump in its Q2 profit, later reported 36.6% annual jump in profit.
Samvardhana Motherson’s net profit increased by 42% on an annual basis to ₹1,175.32 crore, on strong revenue growth.
Uno Minda’s net profit stood at ₹440.81 crore in Q2FY27, up 36.6% from ₹322.79 crore reported in the year-ago period.
Uno Minda’s net revenue increased by 38.2% to ₹6,655.42 crore in the September quarter, up from ₹4,814.03 crore in the year-ago period.
Motilal Oswal increased its target price for Uno Minda to ₹1560 per share, indicating a 17% upside potential in the auto ancillary stock.

items.title: Indian Techie Creates Wildlife Warning System After Losing Mother In Bear Attack
points: Losing a loved one in a wildlife attack can leave a family with unimaginable pain.
But for 33-year-old Indian software engineer Mudasir Ali, the loss of his mother in a bear attack in Kashmir became a reason to use technology to protect others from similar incidents.
He developed an online early-warning system that alerts people about the presence of dangerous wild animals near their homes and other locations.
Ali created Wildping, a free website where people can report sightings of wild animals, including Himalayan black bears and leopards.
According to official data, at least 50 people have been killed, and hundreds more have been injured in wildlife attacks in the region since 2023.

Speaking to AFP, Ali said that after his mother's death, he wanted to use his technical skills to develop something that could help people living in areas where wildlife attacks frequently take place.
It attracted around 9,000 visitors in less than a month, with hundreds of users returning regularly.

items.title: 'Apologise To Ram Bhakts': Yogi Adityanath On Akhilesh Yadav's Ayodhya Temple Visit Plan
points: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday said Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav was welcome to visit Ayodhya but should first apologise to Lord Ram's devotees.

The remark came after the SP announced that Akhilesh Yadav would visit the Ram Temple on December 12, his first visit to the temple that was built around two years ago after decades of litigation over the land where the Babri Masjid was demolished in 1992.
"Those who bloodied Ayodhya are also remembering Ayodhya," Adityanath said at the 10th edition of the Deepotsav, the lighting of thousands of earthen lamps, in Ayodhya.

"Let them come to Ayodhya, but they should seek forgiveness from Ram bhakts (devotees)," Adityanath said, not naming Akhilesh, who was chief minister before Adityanath succeeded him in 2017 as the BJP took power.

items.title: MP Board Class 10, 12 Dummy Admit Card 2027 Out: Check Correction Window Details
points: MP Board 10, 12 Dummy Admit Card 2027: The Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education (MPBSE) has released the dummy admit card for the students appearing for the class 10th and 12th board examinations.
Students can download their dummy admit card from the official MPBSE website, mpbse.mponline.gov.in.
After downloading the hall ticket students are required to verify the details mentioned on it before the release of the final admit card.
With the help of the dummy admit card students and schools can identify the errors, if any, in their examination record and rectify it before the actual exam process.
The deadline for school principals to submit the form is December 31, 2026.

items.title: Ship Captains E-mail Houthis To Obtain Permission For Safe Passage Through Red Sea
points: Yemen’s Houthis have imposed a maritime licensing system in the Red Sea to control commercial shipping traffic through the critical waterway, especially after the Group declared a blockade of Saudi Arabian Ports this year.
According to sources, shipping companies have advised captains of contacting an entity called the Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center or HOOC that was formed by Houthis in 2024.
Through this administrative body, the Houthis give out warnings to ships, and also provide instructions regarding passage and impose shipping restrictions.
Ships send safe-passage requests to this body and according to captains and crew members, the reply from the Houthis comes within 24 hours.

Usually, ships without connections to the U.S, the U.K or Israel don’t need to contact the HOOC for transit requests, however since the declaration of Saudi Arabian port ban by the Group, maritime companies have become vigilant and contact the body for…

items.title: Scientists Crack Code Of 16th Century Brass Lock Recovered From Anne Francis Wreck Off South Wales
points: Scientists used advanced medical imaging technology to crack the four-letter combination of a 16th-century brass padlock that remained buried on a Welsh Beach for almost 400 years.
The lock belonged to Ann Francis, a commercial ship that was wrecked off the coast of South Wales in 1583 after it ran aground due to a powerful storm.
A joint effort between Cardiff University and Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales has successfully revealed the code that once safeguarded the ship captains’ priced possessions.
The high-resolution 3D scans of the lock allowed the researchers to find the code without damaging the relic.

Dr. David Williams, a research associate at Cardiff University’s Musculoskeletal Biomechanics Research Facility, said that by creating 3D images of the lock’s internal mechanism, he could see how the notches matched the letters and find the combination easily.

items.title: Oil Rig Worker Receives 14 Years Jail Sentence For Part In £40 Million Cocaine Smuggling Scheme
points: David Paterson, an oil rig worker from Peterhead was given a 14 year jail sentence by Portsmouth Crown Court for his part in a £40 million cocaine smuggling case, along with 11 others for trying to get 16 bales of class A drugs to the shore.
The National Crime Agency uncovered the network which involved several members involved in smuggling at least 500 kilograms of cocaine.
In August, 2024, Agents waited at the Medmerry Beach, West Sussex as the criminals threw bales into the sea from a container ship.
To prevent water ingress, the drugs were packaged in waterproof wrapping and had a GPS tracker.
They were thrown into the sea, 40 nautical miles south of the Needles, to the west of the Isle of Wight.
The 49-year old Paterson had to recover the drugs from the sea and bring them to shore but he was not successful.

items.title: LA Port Strike Threat Deferred Again As Labor Talks Drag On
points: Shipping containers sit on a Maersk vessel docked at the port of Los Angeles in Long Beach, California, U.S. , March 10, 2026.

REUTERS/Caroline Brehman Nov 7, 2026 (Bloomberg) –The union representing about 250 security workers at the US’s busiest ports agreed to continue negotiations on a new labor contract for two more weeks, their employers said.
20, with additional talks scheduled with the International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 scheduled during that period, the Pacific Maritime Association said in a statement.
Disruptions at the affected terminals could impact roughly 85% of the cargo that moves through the Port of Long Beach and a third of the cargo at the Port of Los Angeles, according to the PMA.

The previous labor contract expired in July 2025, though the PMA, which represents port terminals and ocean carriers, and ILWU Local 26 have been meeting regularly to negotiate with the assistance of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.

items.title: "Warfare No Longer Limited To Cross-Border Firing": Rajnath Singh
points: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said the security landscape had become increasingly complex, with warfare extending beyond conventional cross-border firing to include cyberattacks, drone swarms, proxy wars and information operations.
Addressing Indian Air Force personnel at Bagdogra airfield on the eve of Diwali, Singh said adversaries were increasingly seeking to exploit vulnerabilities without engaging in direct conflict.
"Warfare is no longer limited merely to cross-border firing.
It has expanded greatly to encompass asymmetric warfare, proxy wars, cyberattacks, drone swarms, information operations, and narrative management," he said.

Singh said his visit to the Bagdogra airbase was made with the intent to share his Diwali greetings with the air force personnel and expressed his gratitude to the families of the jawans who remained separated from their loved ones during the festivities.
Singh underscored the strategic importance and sensitivity of the Bagdogra air base, calling it an integral component of India's defence network in overseeing security of the north-eastern region.

items.title: Ahead Of Diwali, UP Hikes Dearness Allowance By 5% For Government Employees
points: The Uttar Pradesh government has announced a Diwali gift for state employees by increasing the dearness allowance (DA) by 5 per cent, raising it from the existing 58 per cent to 63 per cent.

The hike will benefit regular state government employees, full-time employees of aided educational and technical institutions, urban local bodies, acting employees, and those drawing salaries under the University Grants Commission (UGC) pay scale.
The revised DA rate will be effective from July 1, according to a government order issued on Saturday.
The decision is expected to benefit lakhs of employees across the state, providing financial relief to various categories of government and aided institution employees.
According to the government order, provisions have also been made for the payment of arrears arising from the DA hike for the period between July 1 and October 31.
For employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS), 10 per cent of the arrears will be deposited into their Tier-1 pension accounts.

items.title: Soaring Freight Rates Give US Refiners Edge As Crude Discounts Widen

The disruption particularly benefited US Gulf Coast refiners, which could buy discounted heavy crude produced closer to home, including from Canada and Venezuela, while Asian rivals faced sharply higher freight and insurance costs to import similar grades…

Rising freight costs have widened discounts on Canadian heavy crude, including Western Canadian Select (WCS), which typically trades below US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI), creating a windfall for Gulf Coast refiners, as more than 70% of their…

items.title: Biswajit Basu becomes fourth former Calcutta HC judge to quit Bengal SIR tribunal
points: Former Calcutta high court judge Biswajit Basu resigned from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) tribunal on Saturday, citing personal reasons, becoming the fourth judge to step down.
“He submitted his resignation to high court Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, citing personal reasons.

Former high court judge Indrajit Chatterjee quit around 20 days ago, saying he had difficulty travelling more than 20 km every day from his Salt Lake residence to the tribunal in South 24 Parganas district,” a court official said, requesting anonymity.
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ousted the Trinamool Congress (TMC) government in May this year and came to power.

items.title: 2W Retail Sales Oct 2026 – Honda, Hero, TVS, Bajaj, RE, Suzuki, Yamaha, Ather, Ola
points: Two-wheeler retail sales in India witnessed a significant year-on-year (YoY) decline in October 2026, with total registrations falling to 23,21,419 units.
Despite this sharp YoY decline, FADA noted that October 2026 was the second-best October on record for two-wheeler retail sales.
Petrol/ethanol-powered two-wheelers continued to dominate the Indian market, accounting for 90.30% of total retail sales in October 2026.
Total two-wheeler retail sales stood at 23,21,419 units in October 2026, down 28.35% from 32,39,949 units registered in October 2025.
Hero MotoCorp sales declined sharply on a YoY basis to 5,98,433 units from 10,06,796 units of Oct 2025 bringing down its market share to 25.78%.
Combined sales of Honda, Hero and TVS, which stood at 16,94,366 units, accounted for more than 72% of two-wheeler retail market during the month of October 2026.
Bajaj Auto sales fell to 2,09,634 units in Oct 2026 from 3,35,229 units sold in the same month last year RE sales too fell sharply to 1,23,982 units while market share improved to 5.34%.

items.title: Uttarakhand Minister Rekha Arya's Husband Arrested Days After Assault Complaint
points: Uttarakhand Police arrested state Cabinet Minister Rekha Arya's husband, Girdhari Lal Sahu alias Pappu Girdhari, from Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi, officials said on Saturday.
"A case was registered against Girdhari Lal Sahu on October 15, following a complaint filed by the Cabinet Minister, Rekha Arya.

Given the gravity of the matter, a special team was constituted; this nine-member team has now proceeded with the investigation and successfully arrested two key accused: Girdhari Lal Sahu and Satyendra Thakur.

The Cabinet Minister's husband, Girdhari Lal Sahu, was arrested yesterday evening outside a private university campus in the Jhansi district of Uttar Pradesh after he had been on the run for some time.
"Girdhari Lal Sahu has an extensive criminal history; over 44 cases have been registered against him.

items.title: Delhi Air Remains 'Very Poor' On Diwali Eve, Likely To Worsen Tomorrow
points: Delhi's AQI at 369 was in the 'very poor' category on Saturday as smog enveloped the city on the eve of Diwali and reduced visibility.
Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Saturday, air quality remained in the 'severe' category for 16, while for 29, it was in the 'very poor' category.
The worst AQI was recorded near IIT Delhi at 452.
The city's average AQI improved slightly from 382 on Friday to 369 on Saturday, remaining close to the 'severe' threshold of 400.
According to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) for Delhi, the air quality is likely to remain in the 'severe' category on November 8 and 9.

As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.

items.title: Hardeep Puri, Rekha Gupta Meet Victims Of 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots In Delhi
points: Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday met victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots at Puri's residence in Delhi.
During the visit, both Puri and Gupta spoke to victims and enquired about their experiences and well-being.
Visuals showed Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta consoling one of the victims.

This comes as the ruling BJP mounted a counter-offensive to the INDIA bloc's "Chalo Delhi' rally with a march in several zones of the national capital to remember the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of holding a political rally on the…
Puri accused the Congress of deeply hurting Sikh sentiments by staging a political demonstration on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence.
Rejecting the term "riots," Puri classified the 1984 tragedy as an organised "genocide" and a "crime against humanity," citing official figures of 2,733 deaths in Delhi and 3,325 nationwide.
He questioned the official narrative that the 1984 anti-Sikh killings were a spontaneous outbreak of anger following former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's assassination.

items.title: RRC Northern Railway Apprentice Recruitment 2026: Check Vacancy Details, Eligibility
points: The Railway Recruitment Cell (RRC) has released the notification for the Northern Railway Apprentice recruitment 2026.
As per the official notice the vacancies are distributed across six clusters such as Lucknow, Delhi, Ambala, Firozpur, Moradabad and Jammu.
The registration process is set to begin from November 11, 2026 and will continue until December 11, 2026.

Candidates belonging to the General, OBC and EWS category will be required to pay Rs 100 to register for the apprentice recruitment, whereas the SC, ST, PwD and women candidates are exempted from paying the application fee.
Candidates will be selected based on their merit obtained in class 10 and ITI, no written examination or interview will be conducted for the recruitment.
The recruitment drive aims to fill 4,651 apprentice slots across six clusters.
Those applying must be between 15 to 24 years as of December 11, 2026.
A five years of age relaxation is applicable for the SC/ST candidates, following a three years for OBC candidates and 10 years for PwD applicants.

items.title: Tata Motors Offering Discounts Of Up To Rs. 3.35 Lakh On EVs
points: GaadiWaadi - Indian automaker with the widest EV portfolio in the country rolls out offers exceeding Rs 3 lakh on select models Tata Motors has announced several new offers for its electric cars.
The homegrown automaker is giving benefits of up to Rs 3.35 lakh on its EVs this month.
The range starts with the new Tiago.ev, priced from Rs 6.99 lakh (ex-showroom), and ends with the Harrier.ev, which costs Rs 21.79 lakh (ex-showroom) onwards.
It’s been five months since Tata Motors launched the new Tiago.ev, but the old version is still in stock at select dealerships.
The company is giving benefits of up to Rs 1.45 lakh on the old Tiago.ev, including a green bonus of Rs 70,000, an intervention offer of Rs 50,000, and a scrappage bonus of Rs 25,000.
Before the Tiago.ev, Tata Motors rolled out a facelift for the Punch.ev, in February 2026.

points: Here's your 5-minute wrap of the day's top headlines from across the country, the world and the field of sports and entertainment.
The colours of firecrackers in Delhi on Diwali depend on metal salts that burn into fine particles, whether these are the ‘green ones’ or the conventional ones sold illegally.
One of those salts, barium, has been banned in fireworks since 2018.
But, on Diwali night in 2019, a year after the ban, a team from IIT Delhi and other institutes measured barium in Delhi’s air at up to 190 times its level of the week before.
Strontium, which burns red, rose by up to 145 times.

items.title: 22-year-old kills father in Ghaziabad after he scolds him over quarrel with sister: Police
points: A 22-year-old man was arrested after he allegedly killed his 58-year-old father at their home in Loni's Ashok Vihar early on Saturday, police said.
According to the police, the incident took place between 2am and 3am on Saturday while the father and the other family members were asleep.
The police identified the deceased as Mohammad Irfan, 58, while the suspect was identified as Mohammad Shavez, 22.
Later, the elder sister filed a police complaint, following which an FIR was registered against the suspect at Loni police station,” Yogendra Kumar Singh, SHO of Loni, told HT.
“Around 2am on November 7, my brother attacked my father with a sickle or sharp-edged weapon and caused his murder,” the FIR, accessed by HT, said.
Based on the complaint, police registered an FIR against the minor under Section 103(1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at Loni police station on Saturday.
"Initially, the suspect's family told police that he was 15 years old.

items.title: From Green Crackers To Cold Fireworks, The Woman Chasing Smoke-Free Diwali
points: Nine years ago, as Delhi's air turned toxic after Diwali and concerns over pollution mounted across India, a challenge was thrown at Indian scientists.

The challenge came in 2017 from Dr Harsh Vardhan, then Union Minister for Science and Environment and an ENT surgeon by training, who believed science could help preserve tradition while reducing environmental damage.
It was in 2018 that NDTV first exclusively broke the story that India's efforts to develop green crackers had come to fruition.
The first-generation green crackers were developed by a team led by Dr Sadhana Rayalu, then a senior scientist at the National Environment and Engineering Research Institute, Nagpur (CSIR-NEERI).

At the center of this entire story stands Dr Sadhana RayaluPhoto Credit: NDTV Scientists said these changes could reduce particulate emissions by roughly 30 to 40 per cent while still retaining the light and sound effects associated with fireworks.

items.title: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested
points: A dispute over parking space and a dog in Faridabad's Sector 21C turned fatal on Friday night when the former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region was shot dead by his neighbour.
Paramjith Dhankhar, who had returned from Singapore just a day earlier to celebrate Diwali with his family, was shot dead by his neighbour Mohan Sharma after an argument over parking escalated.
Sharma allegedly fired 15 rounds, nine of which hit Dhankhar.
“The suspect is being quizzed and will be produced before a Faridabad court and taken on police-remand for detailed interrogation,” Faridabad ACP (crime) Varun Kumar Dahiya said.
He had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family.
He was also scheduled to attend his nephew’s wedding on November 24.
Dhankar's son Shaurya Dhankhar filed an FIR under section 103(1) (murder) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act was registered at Surajkund police station on Saturday, according to police.
